title: Session amortization & routing playbook for pricing conversations
summary: Quick internal playbook for sales and solutions to explain how Redwood’s runtime reduces per-user session cost by amortizing model work across interactions and routing intelligently to cheaper model variants while protecting latency SLOs.
positioning_claims: Aggregate session-level economics: we price and prove savings at the session level (per end-user interaction) rather than per-token, making ROI relatable to product metrics.
Warm-start amortization: persistent KV/prefix caching + micro-batched warm starts reduce compute per session by 20-50% for typical multi-turn flows.

Routing-based cost control: adaptive routing sends requests to cheaper quantized or trimmed variants unless strict latency/quality requirements demand full model. Net effect: 10-30% lower unit cost with <2% quality delta in most chat workloads.
Predictable SLO tiers: customers can pick p50/p90/p95-backed pricing tiers; our hybrid offering (hosted + reserved pools) prevents surprise tail-cost spikes.
Operational evidence: dashboards surface session amortization rates, hit-rate for cached prefixes, and routing shifts so engineering and finance can reconcile claims quickly.
proof_points: Internal lab: conversational support flow (avg 4 turns) shows 33% token-cost reduction when prefix caching enabled with a 98% cache hit rate for recurring prompts.
Field pilot (mid-market SaaS): routing to quantized v2 for 40% of inference volume produced 18% cost savings with <1.5% drop in NPS-relevant answer quality on our eval set.
Burst smoothing experiment: smoothing microburst spikes reduced p95 tail latency by 120ms and avoided auto-scale cold starts that would have increased hourly spend by 22% during peak windows.
Per-session metric: we track cost-per-active-session, median tokens per session, amortized kernel-seconds per session, and present these on sales one-pagers for easy customer math.
measurement_plan: Define baseline workloads: map 3 representative workloads (support chat, search-renrank, creative writing) and capture token distributions and session lengths.
Metric collection: instrument per-session metrics (session_id, session_length_tokens, cache_hit, routed_variant, latency_ms, cost_microdollars).
A/B experiments: enable prefix caching and routing heuristics for 50% traffic; run for 2 weeks and compute percent reduction in cost-per-session and delta in quality metrics.
Acceptance thresholds: require >=15% reduction in cost-per-session with <=2% regression in chosen quality metric for a win condition.
Rollout plan: stage to hosted customers first (opt-in), then include in Dedicated as a recommended config with telemetry hooks.
competitor_analysis_notes: Vendor A (large cloud managed endpoints): offers aggressive per-token pricing at scale but lacks persistent KV prefix caching and has higher cold-start costs in small-to-medium customers; advantage: broad model catalog and marketplace integrations.
Vendor B (self-hosted runtime): strong cost control via deep quantization but requires expensive ops to maintain stable latencies; customers report 10-30% variance in p95 across traffic shifts.
Open-source runtimes: good at raw throughput benchmarking but typically not integrated with routing/cost policies and enterprise telemetry for per-session reconciliation.
How we differentiate: integrated amortization (caching + batching) + routing policies + pricing tiers + observability (per-session economics) that let GtM tie claims directly to customer KPIs.
sales_scripts: Opening: 'Most vendors talk tokens. You care about users — cost per active session. Here’s how we translate our tech into an apples-to-apples session saving.'
Demo hook: 'We’ll show a real session trace — warm-cache hit, routed to quantized variant on non-critical turn, and the resulting cost delta. You’ll see the session cost drop in real time.'

Objection handling: 'What if quality suffers?' -> 'We gate routing with eval-driven thresholds and fall back to higher fidelity models whenever our quality monitors detect drift. Field pilots show <2% quality delta on standard helpdesk flows.'
Procurement ask: 'If you want a predictable bill, pick a p95 SLO tier and reserved capacity; we’ll provide a forecasted cost-per-session range based on your observed session profiles.'
Close: 'We can run a 2-week pilot with your real traffic — if we don’t deliver the agreed cost-per-session improvement, we’ll provide credits and a rollback plan.'
customer_examples_and_math: Example A (support chat): avg 4 turns, baseline tokens/session = 1,200, baseline cost/session = $0.018. With caching + routing we reduce tokens/compute equivalent to $0.012 -> 33% saving. Projected annual saving for 100k sessions/day = ~$219k.

Example B (embedded search + rerank): rerank stage amortization reduces model calls per search by 0.6 calls on average -> 20% reduction in per-query cost; show math in deal decks with ARR sensitivity table.
Note: always present conservative and aggressive scenarios; customers prefer conservative numbers during procurement.
operational_notes_for_solutions: Pre-reqs: route-aware routing table, prefix cache enabled, telemetry hooks to export per-session metrics to customer BI or our console.
Config knobs: cache TTL, max-prefix-size, quantized-fraction (percent of traffic eligible for quantized variant), latency-safety-margin (ms).
Instrumentation: ensure session identifiers persist across retries so amortization is correctly attributed; correlate with billing pipeline for verification.
Escalation runbook: if quality regressions > threshold, auto-disable routing and notify SE + customer success with a trace link.
open_questions: How do we standardize 'active session' definition across customers with different UX (chat vs ephemeral prompts)?
What minimum telemetry retention (days) do sales need to validate pilot claims during procurement?
Should we offer an explicit ‘amortization SLA’ as a premium add-on or keep it implicit inside SLO tiers?
How to price when customers want guaranteed % of traffic always on quantized variant vs dynamic routing?
